doc.title: Jake Hanna interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997

title: Cruise ship with Conte Candoli and Carl Fontana
summary: Playing three times a day on a ship; Candoli and Fontana's jokes.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Oh, yeah. Man he’s really got a good ear too. But do you believe Conte Candoli in there tonight? I never heard music like that for years, except out of him. Boy was he playing, ooh, man. Some player that guy. Some player. We were on a ship, Carl Fontana and him and Pete, his brother Pete, and Bob Cooper was alive then, Bob was playing, myself, Randy Sandke, Ross Tompkins. Yeah, they worked us a little too much on this boat you know. We were supposed to go once then back. But we were playing three times a day, and nobody ever showed up. But we were eating. Oh first, we got off the boat. We got off the boat. They’re two idiots these guys, Carl Fontana and Candoli. Turner stood there “look at this big ship.” The Ensenada. [inaudible] He says “Count” Conte Candoli “Count” he says. “Is thata you boat out there?” He says “Insanada ma boat.” These two — we had to put up with these two all week long. And at suppertime we were eating and you had to write down what you thought of the food. I said excellent, excellent, everything was great, don’t bother me. Count says “the food is terrible and the portions are too small.” He’s a funny guy. Oh, he’s funny.
